tagline: Building great companies for the long term
hero_kpi_rationale: NAV per Share is the master KPI for Exor because it is a holding company whose value is determined by the performance of its strategic investments, particularly Ferrari. This KPI directly captures shareholder value creation.
company_description: Exor N.V. engages in the automotive, agriculture and construction, sports car, commercial vehicle, health technology, football and powertrain businesses in the Netherlands and internationally. The company designs, engineers, produces, and sells luxury performance sports cars under the Ferrari brand. It also provides automotive vehicles and mobility solutions under the Abarth, Alfa Romeo, Chrysler, Citroen, Dodge, DS, Fiat, Fiat Professional, Jeep, Lancia, Maserati, Mopar, Opel, Peugeot, Ram, and Vauxhall brands; diagnostic imaging, ultrasound, image-guided therapy, monitoring and enterprise informatic, and personal health equipment under Philips brand; agricultural and construction equipment and services; heavy, medium, and light-duty trucks; powertrain technologies; mass-transit and premium buses and coaches; defense and civil protection equipment; heavy-duty quarry and construction vehicles; and firefighting vehicles and equipment, as well as financing services. In addition, the company offers men's footwear, leather goods, beauty, and accessories; equipment for the building and repairing of oil and gas wells; clean energy solutions; data, insights and analytics, expert, and work

kpis.name: Net Asset Value per Share
kpis.explanation: Total value of assets minus liabilities, divided by the number of shares.
kpis.description: Net asset value per share increased by 9.0% in 2024, driven by Ferrari's performance, despite underperforming the MSCI World.
kpis.signal: Solid growth despite a difficult market.

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Consolidated EBITDA margin of portfolio companies, calculated as EBITDA divided by revenues.
kpis.description: Ferrari's EBITDA margin reached 38% in 2024, reflecting its industrial strength and premium positioning.

kpis.name: Consolidated Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated by key portfolio companies, primarily Ferrari.
kpis.description: Ferrari generated €6.7 billion in revenue in 2024, up 12%, driven by new product launches and strong demand.

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, primarily from Ferrari.
kpis.description: Ferrari delivered €2.6 billion in EBITDA in 2024, confirming its operational strength.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €37.13 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €3.67 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Leapmotor Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by Leapmotor, a joint venture with Stellantis, specializing in electric vehicles in China.
kpis.description: Leapmotor exceeded €4 billion in revenue in 2024, with over 90% growth and an 8.4% gross margin, achieving profitability in Q4.
kpis.signal: Explosive growth of Leapmotor in the Chinese EV market.

kpis.name: Stellantis Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues of Stellantis, one of Exor's key assets and a global leader in the automotive industry.
kpis.description: Stellantis saw revenues decline to €156.9 billion in 2024 (-17% vs 2023), impacted by weak industry volumes, Chinese competition, and internal operational challenges.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in 2024 due to external and internal challenges.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Total amount paid in dividends per share over the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Capital returned to shareholders
kpis.explanation: Annual total: dividends paid + share buybacks.
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends and buybacks (2021-2025) in billion EUR. Source yfinance cashflow.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Portion of net income redistributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2020-2024). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Electric transition and uncertain EV demand
risks.summary: Stellantis faces weaker-than-expected EV demand in 2024-2025, exacerbated by regulatory uncertainty and reduced government incentives. The transition to electric vehicles creates temporary gaps in the product lineup and forces aggressive discounts to clear inventory.
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for Stellantis (40% of portfolio). Explicitly mentioned as a key factor in 2024 decline: « regulatory uncertainty, increased customer price sensitivity and reduced government incentives for EVs ». Intense language (« challenging », « struggling »). Risk trend increasing with pause of Ram electric. Critical weight in transition strategy.

risks.title: Increased competition from Chinese automakers
risks.summary: Chinese automotive manufacturers are capturing significant market share with low-priced electric vehicles, particularly in Brazil, the EU and Mexico. This competition exerts downward pricing pressure and reduces demand for established automakers, forcing Stellantis to invest in JVs like Leapmotor to remain competitive.
risks.score_rationale: Existential risk for Stellantis and CNH. Precise data: « Chinese exports of electric passenger vehicles in 2024 totalled 1.3 million units, a year-on-year increase of 24% ». Alarmist language (« intensified competition », « exerted downward pressure »). Risk trend increasing with penetration in Brazil, EU, Mexico. Direct impact on pricing and volumes.

risks.title: Product liability litigation and mass recalls
risks.summary: Philips resolved major litigation related to the Respironics recall (Sleep & Respiratory Care) in 2024 with total payments of $1.1 billion in the U.S. and €540 million to insurers. Although largely resolved, residual product liability risks remain in the highly regulated medical sector.
risks.score_rationale: Philips had to pay $1.1 billion + €540 million for the Respironics recall. Mentioned as « significant milestones » but remains a residual risk. Moderate language (« resolved », « clarity ») but substantial amounts. Risk trend stable with ongoing resolution. Important weight for Philips (10% of GAV).

risks.title: Agricultural cyclicality and falling commodity prices
risks.summary: CNH faces a downturn in agriculture and construction, with farmers experiencing reduced incomes (lower commodity prices, high input costs). Combine harvester sales fell 43% in EMEA and 31% in South America in 2024.
risks.score_rationale: CNH experienced a 23% sales decline in 2024. Explicit language: « cyclical downturn », « reduced incomes driven by lower commodity prices ». Regional data: Brazil and Europe weak, combines down 43% in EMEA. Risk trend increasing. Significant weight (CNH in portfolio).

risks.title: Post-acquisition integration and operational issues
risks.summary: Clarivate struggles to integrate prior acquisitions and maintain innovation, while Stellantis faces production delays due to large-scale factory retooling for new platforms. These operational issues limit the ability to meet demand and impact margins.
risks.score_rationale: Clarivate suffers from « integration issues from its previous strategy » and Stellantis from « large-scale retooling of factories ». Moderate but repeated language (« struggling », « gaps in product lineup »). Risk trend increasing with CEO change at Clarivate. Moderate but growing weight.

risks.title: Dependence on leadership and succession risks
risks.summary: Exor had to manage several key leadership changes in 2024 (Stellantis, CNH, Clarivate), reflecting operational challenges. While new leaders bring expertise, transitions create execution and strategic continuity risks.
risks.score_rationale: Carlos Tavares resigned in December 2024 at Stellantis; Gerrit Marx appointed CEO of CNH in July 2024; Matti Shem Tov appointed CEO of Clarivate in August 2024. Neutral language but frequent changes. Risk trend increasing with 3 CEO changes in 6 months. Moderate but strategic weight.

risks.title: Slowdown in Chinese market and post-COVID normalization
risks.summary: The Chinese healthcare market slowed in 2024, with luxury down (~20%) and post-pandemic normalization affecting bioMérieux and Philips. This slowdown reduces growth prospects in a key market for the healthcare sector.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned for bioMérieux and Philips: « softness in the Chinese market and further post-COVID normalisation led to weaker results ». Moderate language (« difficult year »). Risk trend stable but persistent. Moderate weight for healthcare portfolio.

risks.title: Saturation and competition in data and software
risks.summary: Clarivate faces increased competition across its three segments (Academia, IP, Lifesciences) and a slowdown in end markets, particularly in IP where filings and renewals are below historical trends.
risks.score_rationale: Clarivate faces « ever-growing competition in all its markets » and end-market slowdown (IP filings, biotech funding). Moderate language (« facing challenges »). Risk trend increasing with 40% share price drop in 2024. Moderate weight (growth investment).

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence in the 2024 annual report. Exor does not position AI as a strategic lever for its companies.
evidence: No reference to AI or related technologies in strategy or innovation sections.
No KPI or initiative linked to AI is mentioned.
Technology discussions focus on electrification, vehicle platforms and product innovation (F80, Ferrari 12Cilindri, e-building).
